sentences: Cutting Planes refutes unsatisfiable Boolean formulas using linear inequalities and arithmetic inference.
The saved question asks whether every unsatisfiable CNF has such a refutation using linear total space.
Total space accounts for the information simultaneously stored, making coefficient encoding potentially relevant.
An affirmative result would show that powerful arithmetic reasoning can always be carried out with modest memory, regardless of proof length.
The excerpt does not define the reference input-size measure or coefficient accounting, so those conventions are still required before interpreting the linear bound precisely.
